title: 15m Supertrend(10,3) up-flip above the closed-1h EMA200, Supertrend-line stop, 2R target, 24-hour time exit

source.title: SuperTrade ST1 (StockSharp API examples: Supertrend 10/3 with EMA200 filter on 15-minute candles)

rule_summary: Chart 15m, closed bars; signal at bar close, fill at next bar open; long only, one position. 15m indicators: ATR10 = Wilder ATR(10); Supertrend with factor 3 on hl2 = (high+low)/2: basic upper = hl2 + 3*ATR10, basic lower = hl2 - 3*ATR10, with the standard ratchet (final lower band can only rise while close stays above it, final upper band can only fall while close stays below it); direction turns UP when close crosses above the final upper band and DOWN when close crosses below the final lower band; the Supertrend line is the final lower band in UP direction. 1h filter: EMA200 of 1h closes, using only the last COMPLETED 1h bar (informative 1h, merged so no partial bar is seen). ENTRY at close of 15m bar t when direction(t-1) = DOWN, direction(t) = UP, close(t) > EMA200_1h, and no position. At entry store S = Supertrend line at t (fixed stop) and R = entry fill - S; skip the trade if R/entry < 0.004. EXITS (first hit): stop at S (intrabar); take-profit limit at entry + 2R; 15m direction flips to DOWN (exit next open); time exit at the close of the 96th 15m bar after entry (24 hours).
mechanism: Short-horizon trend continuation: a Supertrend flip needs a close more than 3 ATRs from the bar midpoint against the prior trend, i.e. a move that forces late shorts and passive sellers to reprice; the closed-1h EMA200 keeps only flips in the direction of the slower trend, where breakouts are less often faded by mean-reversion liquidity providers. Same rule (15m Supertrend 10/3, EMA200 filter) is described by FMZ strategy 486561 (15m Supertrend + 1h EMA200, stop at the Supertrend line, risk-reward target) and by marketcalls.in (Supertrend with EMA filter, long-only, 15m). The stop sits about 1-3 ATR15 below entry, so the 2R target is usually 1-3% away, several times the 0.30-0.45% round trip; the 0.4% minimum risk keeps the target at or above 0.8%.
